title: Giving Compliments
summary: We practised giving compliments and answering them politely. We learned the structure have/get something done for things other people do for us. We also practised the vowel sounds in positive adjectives.

vocab.example: She gave me a lovely compliment about my new haircut.

grammar.title: have / get something done
grammar.explain: We use have/get + object + past participle when another person does a job for us, usually because we pay them. 'Get' is more informal than 'have'. Compare: 'I cut my hair' (I did it myself) and 'I had my hair cut' (a hairdresser did it).
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم have/get + المفعول به + التصريف الثالث للفعل عندما يقوم شخص آخر بعمل لنا، وغالباً ندفع له مقابل ذلك. كلمة get أقل رسمية من have. قارن: 'I cut my hair' تعني أنني قصصت شعري بنفسي، أما 'I had my hair cut' فتعني أن الحلاق قصّه لي.
form: have + object + past participle: I had my hair done.
get + object + past participle (more informal): I got my hair done.
Change the tense of have/get: I'm having my eyes tested tomorrow. / I need to get a spare key made.
Question: Did you have/get your hair cut? Where do you get your shoes repaired?

examples.en: Helen had her hair done before her friend's birthday party.
examples.note: A hairdresser did Helen's hair, not Helen.

examples.en: Helen put her make-up on before the party.
examples.note: Helen did it herself, so we do not use have/get done.

examples.en: Did you get your hair cut? It looks really stylish!
examples.note: A common way to start a compliment.

examples.en: Where is the best place to get your eyes tested?
examples.note: An optician tests your eyes for you.

examples.en: I need to have a passport photo taken.

mistakes.wrong: I cut my hair at the salon yesterday.
mistakes.right: I had my hair cut at the salon yesterday.
mistakes.why: 'I cut my hair' means you did it yourself. Use have/get + object + past participle when someone else does it.
The object (my hair) goes between have and the past participle.
Use the past participle (repaired), not the base form.

mistakes.wrong: Did you do your nails done?
mistakes.right: Did you have/get your nails done?
mistakes.why: The verb is have or get, not do.

quiz.q: Your hair looks great! Did you ___ it done at the salon?
quiz.why: get + object + past participle: get it done.

quiz.q: I'm going to have my car ___ tomorrow.
quiz.why: After have + object we use the past participle.

quiz.q: Which sentence means a hairdresser did it?
quiz.why: have + object + past participle = someone else did it for her.

quiz.q: I need to ___ a spare key made.
quiz.why: get + object (a spare key) + past participle (made).

quiz.q: Helen ___ her make-up on herself before the party.
quiz.why: She did it herself, so we use the normal verb, not have/get done.

grammar.title: Compliment patterns: What (a/an) + adjective + noun!
grammar.explain: To give a strong compliment we can say 'What + a/an + adjective + singular noun!' With plural or uncountable nouns we drop a/an. We can also use 'You look + adjective', 'That ... really suits you' and 'You've got + adjective + noun'.
grammar.explain_ar: لإعطاء مجاملة قوية نقول: What + a/an + صفة + اسم مفرد! ومع الأسماء الجمع أو غير المعدودة نحذف a/an. ويمكننا أيضاً استخدام You look + صفة، و That ... really suits you، و You've got + صفة + اسم.
form: What + a/an + adjective + singular noun! (What a beautiful dress!)
What + adjective + plural / uncountable noun! (What fantastic glasses!)
That colour/coat really suits you. / That ... looks amazing on you.
You've got + adjective + noun. (You've got pretty eyes.)

examples.en: What an amazing hat you're wearing!
examples.note: 'an' because 'amazing' starts with a vowel sound.

examples.en: That colour looks great on you.
You've got a great sense of style.
You look younger with short hair.

mistakes.why: 'top' is a singular noun, so we need 'a'.
'Small' is about size. For age, use 'young'.

mistakes.wrong: All of people say that to me.
It's a good thing or a bad thing?
mistakes.right: Is it a good thing or a bad thing?
mistakes.why: In questions, put the verb before the subject.

quiz.why: 'dress' is a singular noun and 'lovely' starts with a consonant sound.
'unusual' starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an'.

options: You've got a great sense of style.
quiz.why: The other two are negative and should be avoided.

options: All of people say that to me.
All people says that to me.
